text: Structure: two-compartment (WSS one-compartment 13.870 [Hessian PD TRUE], two-compartment 1.596 [Hessian PD TRUE]; two-compartment adopted only if WSS drops by > 5.99); see pk_structure_summary.csv and pk_structure_comparison.csv | C24 (24 h after the acute dose): observed NTX 2.1, BN 17.6 ng/mL; one-compartment predicts NTX 2.95, BN 21.87; two-compartment predicts NTX 2.10, BN 21.72. At least one structure reproduces both 24 h values within a factor of 1.5. | Objective statistics: C24, Cmax, thalf, Tmax; CV floor 0.10 (Tmax 0.25) | Final WSS 1.5960; Hessian eigenvalues (of hessian/2): 155.2, 116, 35.39, 18.57, 13.28, 4.085, 0.4757; positive definite: TRUE | ka 1.860 per h (absorption half-life 22.4 min) | Observations 12 (8 single-dose, 4 once-daily at steady state; regimen column of pk_summary.csv) and 12 nominally distinct (regimen, analyte, stat) combinations, but only 11 distinct predicted values to 6 significant figures and 10 to 3 (the single-dose and steady-state terminal half-lives are the same quantity in a linear model: NTX coincides exactly, BN to 0.1%). With 7 fitted parameters: nominal residual degrees of freedom 5, EFFECTIVE 4 (3 at 3 significant figures). | Tmax check: NTX observed 1.00 h, predicted 1.00 h; BN observed 2.00 h, predicted 1.96 h | Parent naltrexone disposition half-lives: distribution 1.23 h, terminal 9.79 h; smallest Hessian eigenvalue 0.476 (largest 155) | Fixed parameters: fp fixed at 0.95: the approved naltrexone labelling gives oral bioavailability of 5 to 40 per cent, i.e. a systemic parent fraction (1 - fp) of roughly 0.05 to 0.40; 0.95 sits at the UPPER EDGE of that range (1 - fp = 0.05) and inside the region where the weighted SSE is flat (change <= 0.29 for fp 0.9 to 0.999 in the free fit). Occupancy sensitivity at fp = 0.90 and 0.99 is reported (pk_fit_sens_fp090.rds, pk_fit_sens_fp099.rds) and is immaterial (occupancy moves by at most 0.001). | Limitation (stated; no structure added): the chronic (once-daily, steady-state) 6-beta-naltrexol Cmax is under-predicted, 103.7 vs observed 158.4 ng/mL (0.65-fold). With the 24 h concentrations in the fit, linear kinetics cannot also produce the observed 1.8-fold rise of the chronic over the acute peak; Verebey 1976 itself reports no trough accumulation. The observation's CV (0.57) keeps its weight low. | Unbound fraction of 6-beta-naltrexol: fu_BN = 0.79 is taken EQUAL TO THE PARENT's fu_NTX by fallback: no 6-beta-naltrexol plasma-protein-binding value was found (data/README.md 'Not found' list). It is an assumption, not a measurement, and it scales every unbound 6-beta-naltrexol concentration.

Posterior parameters are labelled prior-determined when posterior SD / prior SD >= 0.9 (computed in scripts/11_tables.R from training_fit.csv and the priors; R/reporting.R), otherwise fitted. 20 of 30 posterior rows are prior-determined.
pbo_emax_logit (Byon 2010) is curated in data/priors/placebo_priors.csv for reference only and is used by no code.

Binding stage J adopted (stage_decision.csv): Stage A (bottom-up, no PET row fitted) is the genuine held-out PET test and fails it: RMSE 31.4 points on all 11 rows (weighted SSE 108.6), implied single-dose occupancy ED50 0.55 mg vs Rabiner 2011 5.60 mg (3.65-7.54). Stage A2 (one Kd scale 9.82 fitted to the six Rabiner rows only) fits those rows (RMSE 7.2) but not the Lee 1988 duration rows (all-row RMSE 33.8, weighted SSE 145.9), because its koff is unchanged; kept as a sensitivity bound. Stage J fits a shared Kd scale (1.60, SE of log 0.363) and a shared koff scale (0.0020, SE of log 0.266) jointly to all 11 rows, precision-weighted (weighted SSE 11.9, RMSE 10.1; Hessian positive definite). keq sensitivity: no keq value lowers the weighted SSE by more than 3.84 (the chi-square(1) 95% point) relative to the default 2 per h (largest gain 2.96, at keq = 8): default kept. Stage J is adopted because it is the only stage consistent with both the potency (Rabiner) and the duration (Lee) data. It uses the PET data for calibration after bottom-up prediction failed, so it is post-hoc and exploratory, and PET is no longer a held-out test for the adopted stage; the Rabiner ED50 comparison is not independent for A2 or J (it summarises scans used to calibrate them).
